challenges.title: A tiny IoC container with constructor injection
challenges.prompt: Write a mini dependency-injection container in plain Java: map interfaces to implementations, create beans by resolving constructor parameters recursively, cache singletons and detect missing beans and circular dependencies with clear messages. This models what Spring's ApplicationContext does; it uses only the JDK, and Spring itself was not run.
challenges.expected:
Hello, Ana
same instance: true, shared audit: true
[run Ana]
no bean for Greeter
circular dependency: A -> B -> A
challenges.explain: Reflection reads each constructor's parameter types and get() resolves them recursively. A stack of types being resolved reveals cycles, and the singleton map gives Spring's default scope. Verified by compiling and running with Java 20; real Spring adds scopes, lifecycle callbacks and proxies.

challenges.title: Retry with backoff and a circuit breaker
challenges.prompt: Combine retries (exponential backoff) with a circuit breaker that opens after repeated failures, allows one half-open probe after a cool-down and closes again on success. A fake clock makes the run deterministic. This is a plain-Java model of what Resilience4j provides in a Spring Boot service; no real service or Spring was involved.
challenges.expected:
gave up: circuit open
attempt 1 failed (boom1), waiting 100ms
attempt 2 failed (boom2), waiting 200ms
attempt 3 failed (boom3), waiting 400ms
state=OPEN calls=3 t=700
half-open probe failed: circuit open, state=OPEN
ok
state=CLOSED calls=5 t=2800
challenges.explain: The breaker counts consecutive failures, opens, and after openMs lets a single probe through; a failed probe re-opens it while a success closes it. retry() stops immediately when the circuit is open instead of waiting. Verified by compiling and running with Java 20.
